summary: a batch's spans reach one candidate and are gated once over it, and with the last engine pick onto trunk go the reset, the abort and the bystander checkpoint
acceptance: a batch picks every span onto one candidate at the trunk tip and gates it once — green ships them in one ledger commit and one fast-forward, red or a conflict discards it and merges the spans one at a time — and the primary checkout hosts no cherry-pick, abort, reset or checkpoint of the engine's
tests: a batch's spans are picked in order onto one candidate and gated once over it
a green batch ships every span in one ledger commit and one fast-forward
a red batch discards its candidate and merges its spans one at a time
pins: a conflict while picking a batch discards the candidate and the spans are carried serially
notes: `carryMergeBatch` picks onto trunk and `reset --keep`s back; its `unwound` fate exists only for that reset, and a refused unwind throws and walls the wave. The shared pick also holds the checkpoint and the abort, so converting it frees `resetKeepTo`, `cherryPickAbort`, `checkpointBystanderState` and `checkMergedTipUnmoved` — the export pin reds unless they go in the same commit. Not contract-touching: this repo declares no `mergeBatch`, so the path is dormant and only the suite drives it.

interface.changes: nothing a caller calls: the tick verdict stops carrying a bystander checkpoint sha, because no engine write reaches the operator's tree for one to recover
interface.hides: that an engine merge can touch uncommitted work at all, and the recovery handle an operator was owed for it
interface.rejected: keeping the checkpoint as cheap insurance — an unreachable recovery handle is dead plumbing, and the verdict field would read as a promise the engine no longer makes
